evals.prompt: our CI suite fails maybe 1 in 5 runs and its always a different test. everyone just hits re-run until it goes green. this is driving me nuts, where do i even start
evals.expected_output: Treats flakiness as a defect with causes to diagnose rather than something to retry around, and names the usual culprits (fixed sleeps instead of waiting on a condition, wall-clock or timezone dependence, unguaranteed iteration order, shared state between concurrently running tests, real network calls). Explains why retry logic makes it worse by masking real failures and corrupting the measurement. Proposes a concrete way to identify which tests actually flake before fixing anything.

evals.prompt: we're adding a discount code field to checkout. QA wants a playwright test for it. we already have 40 e2e tests and the suite takes 25 minutes
evals.expected_output: Does not simply write the requested end-to-end test. Asks what this test would protect that a cheaper test would not, and concludes that discount code validation belongs at a lower level - the rule itself as a unit test, the apply-to-cart wiring as an integration test - with end-to-end reserved for the journey where the integration is the thing at risk. Names the cost of a 41st journey test against a 25 minute suite, and offers the one end-to-end assertion worth keeping if any. Does not treat the QA request as settled just because it was asked for.

evals.prompt: our e2e suite is the only thing catching bugs but it's slow and breaks constantly. half the failures are 'element not found' after a css change. should we just delete it?
evals.expected_output: Separates two problems: the suite is doing work that belongs at lower levels, and the tests it does keep are written against markup rather than against the journey. Recommends pushing assertions down rather than deleting outright, since deleting removes the only signal currently working. Addresses selector strategy (accessible name and role over css), waiting on conditions rather than durations, and test-owned data. Keeps a small number of journeys and says how to choose them.
